raw_response:
I'm 65, been farming this same 4.5 mu in Quzhou since I was 20. Never went to school — can't read a word — but I know this land better than any book. Me and the old lady, just the two of us now. Our children are off in Shijiazhuang working factory jobs. They send a little money back now and then, but not much. So this cotton patch is still our rice bowl.

This year, same as last year, all 4.5 mu goes to cotton. I thought about wheat-corn double crop when I was younger, but at my age, with just two of us, that turnaround in June is too much. Cotton is slower. You plant in April, pick through September and October. We can handle the pace.

For seed, I'll buy from the supply shop in town — the same improved variety my neighbors use, the ones with the pink coating. About one jin per mu, costs around 45 yuan per mu. I stopped saving my own seed years ago; the bought seedlings grow stronger and more even.

Fertilizer is the big worry. Prices keep going up. Last year I put down two big bags of compound fertilizer — the one with the three numbers on the bag, I don't know what they mean — and one and a half bags of urea for the whole 4.5 mu. I spread the compound before planting, then sidedressed the urea when the flowers opened in July. The cotton did fine, got about the same yield as always. Old Zhang down the lane tried to save money by cutting back to one bag of compound last year, and his plants were yellow and stunted. So I'm not cutting back. I'll do the same as last year: two bags compound, one and a half bags urea. It's a lot of money up front, but if I under-fertilize and the yield drops, that's worse than wasting a bit of fertilizer. Better safe than sorry.

I'll irrigate twice from the well: once when flowering starts around early July, and once when the bolls are filling in August. Pumping costs electricity, so I don't water more than I have to. If we get good rain, maybe I'll skip the second one. Cotton doesn't like wet feet.

Pests are always trouble. I'll spray four or five times this season — once with herbicide before planting to kill the weeds, then insecticide for aphids when the seedlings are up, and three more times for bollworm when the buds and bolls form. The shop has that red-capped bottle, about 20 yuan a spray. Can't skip it — one bad bollworm year and you lose half the crop.

For tillage, I'll hire Young Liu to bring his walking tractor and rotary-till the field. Costs about 30 yuan per mu. I sold my own tractor five years ago when my back got too bad.

Labor is tight. Me and the old lady can handle the planting, spraying, and running the pump. But picking is the killer — cotton picking will break your back. For 4.5 mu, we'll need to hire women from the village to help with the main picking. They usually get paid by the jin. Between us and the hired hands, we'll get it all in.

I'm expecting about the same yield as last year — around 240 kg per mu, maybe a bit more if the weather treats us well. I've seen good years and bad years. At my age, I don't gamble. I do what worked before, watch what my neighbors do, and don't try anything fancy.
